title: Adaptive damage-rate cap
subtitle: Limit burst damage without turning the boss invulnerable
summary: Recent or estimated burst damage lowers the fraction of each new hit that reaches the boss, then the attenuation relaxes when the damage window clears.
overview: A damage-rate cap protects encounter structure from extreme burst while ordinary attacks still move the health bar. It estimates pressure with a recent-damage window or weapon-DPS model, then reduces later damage above a threshold. Define the window, curve, floor, decay, exception order, and feedback so stronger builds still feel effective.
learning: Define the measured damage sample, window duration, threshold, attenuation curve, minimum multiplier, per-hit and damage-type exceptions, first-hit behavior, decay, phase resets, multiplayer aggregation, health application order, stable hit ids, rollback, and telemetry for raw, applied, and prevented damage.

demo.title: Compare an isolated sword hit with a rapid burst, then wait for the cap to recover
demo.step: Isolated hit, attenuated burst, decay, and restored hit
phaseDescriptions: Tavi lands an isolated 18-point sword hit at 0.92 s. With no recent damage in the window, all 18 points apply and Kern falls from 100 to 82 health.
A four-hit burst begins at 2.08 s. The same raw 18-point hit first applies 18, then only 9, 6, and 5 as the recent-damage meter fills; Kern reaches 44 instead of 10.
The meter drains from 3.48 to 4.48 s. A new 18-point hit at 4.94 s again applies the full 18, proving that the rule paces damage rather than creating invulnerability.
demo.danger: Every hit still resolves once; only its applied amount changes from the measured pressure, curve, and floor
demo.locked: Window membership, threshold, multiplier, exception order, phase reset, multiplayer ownership, rollback, and health mutation belong to encounter logic
demo.safe: Show raw versus applied damage, the recent-damage window, changing protection, and the exact boss-health result
demo.reducedMotion: Autoplay is disabled by reduced motion. Scrub across 0.34, 0.92, 1.72, 2.08, 2.43, 2.78, 3.13, 3.48, 4.48, 4.94, and 5.42 seconds to inspect the curve and reset.
demo.diagramDescription: Tavi strikes Kern once for full damage, then performs a rapid series whose equal raw hits shrink as a recent-damage meter fills. After the meter drains, one more equal hit deals full damage again.

steps.title: What pressure does the rule measure?
steps.body: Choose a rolling sum, weighted history, weapon burst-DPS estimate, or another explicit sample. Record which hits enter it, when they expire, whether players share a window, and whether the current hit is evaluated before or after it is added.

steps.title: How does pressure change a hit?
steps.body: Map measured pressure to a multiplier with a documented threshold, curve, and nonzero floor. Keep identical input deterministic, clamp the result once, and decide the order of critical hits, armor, vulnerabilities, shields, and attenuation.

steps.title: How does the player read and test it?
steps.body: Make applied damage, health loss, and recovery from attenuation distinguishable. Test isolated hits, dense bursts, damage-over-time, multihit attacks, multiplayer focus fire, phase transitions, latency, duplicate events, and builds on both sides of the threshold.

mistakes.title: More power produces the same result with no explanation
mistakes.body: If numbers, reactions, and health loss do not reveal attenuation, players read the system as a bug or dishonest scaling. Preserve meaningful gains below and above the threshold and expose the changed multiplier through feedback or encounter UI.

mistakes.title: The cap becomes a hidden invulnerability phase
mistakes.body: A near-zero floor, long memory, or reset that never arrives can erase valid play. Give the window a bounded lifetime, maintain a useful minimum contribution, and audit interactions that continuously refresh pressure.

designNotes.title: Keep the damage transaction ordered
designNotes.body: For each hit, store hitId, sourceId, rawDamage, recentSample, threshold, multiplier, appliedDamage, preventedDamage, healthBefore, healthAfter, and resolution time. Replayed hit ids must not apply twice.

designNotes.title: Decide what skill the cap rewards
designNotes.body: A rolling window can reward cadence and intentional pauses; a weapon-DPS model can equalize loadouts but may feel detached from moment-to-moment play. Pick the model that protects the encounter without invalidating the combat verbs you want players to express.

designNotes.title: Measure the compression, not only completion
designNotes.body: Track raw-to-applied ratio, time above threshold, damage prevented per source, kill time by build, phase skips, first-hit spikes, multiplayer concentration, floor uptime, and whether players recognize why their numbers changed.

story.title: Kern’s runes harden under a flurry
story.body: One measured cut crosses the elemental’s shell cleanly. When Tavi crowds several blows together, the runes flare and spread the force across the stone; after a quiet beat their glow fades and the blade bites deeply again.

adaptation.title: Expose pressure and recovery through more than numbers
adaptation.body: Combine health-bar motion, hit sound, impact weight, color, controller feedback, a protection aura, and an optional recent-damage meter. Offer a gentler curve, shorter window, higher floor, or explicit threshold indicator without changing which events qualify.

distinction.title: Adaptive attenuation, not armor, a hit cap, or a health gate
distinction.body: Armor reduces damage by a mostly stable rule, a per-hit cap clips one large hit, and a health gate stops progress at a fixed boundary. A damage-rate cap changes later hits according to recent or estimated pressure and relaxes when that pressure decays.

lensNotes.body: Raw damage, applied damage, the recent-pressure meter, and health loss must explain why progress compresses during a burst and returns afterward.
Continuing a burst maintains pressure and tempo but accepts lower efficiency; pausing restores efficiency at the cost of time and possibly position.
First hits, criticals, damage-over-time, multihit attacks, phase resets, multiplayer focus fire, and duplicate callbacks need explicit ordering.
The curve decides whether burst builds, sustained damage, coordinated volleys, and deliberate cadence remain meaningfully distinct.
Window length and decay create a combat rhythm of pressure and release that should align with openings instead of fighting them.

examples.body: From 2:00, Hush’s second form demonstrates a long encounter protected from extreme burst. Its documented Damage Scaling tracks unmodified damage over the previous four seconds and lowers the multiplier toward a floor, making window length and minimum contribution central tuning values.

At 7:42, an extreme first-hit setup defeats Archon Boreal despite the encounter’s Damage Attenuation. The exception is useful design evidence: initialization and operation order matter as much as the curve, because a spike evaluated before enough pressure exists can bypass the intended pacing.

The boss fight begins at 11:00. The Fragmented One is documented with Damage Attenuation and a maximum DPS amount; the sustained firefight shows why designers must validate the cap across continuous weapons, high fire rates, status effects, and a long health-bar read rather than only single attacks.
